title: Wing Lower Cover Stringer Run-Outs Ribs 8 to 14 — Ultrasonic Inspection

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Ultrasonic inspection from inside the tank of the stringer run-out region between ribs 8 and 14 on the four-engine stretched aircraft, with the fastener-by-fastener recording that the fatigue assessment depends on.

sections.purpose: This task finds and sizes fatigue cracking at the run-out of stringers 12 through 18 on the wing lower cover between ribs 8 and 14, and records the result in the form the fatigue assessment needs.
sections.job_setup_note: This is a tank entry task. The aircraft must be de-fuelled and the tank purged, and the atmosphere test must be complete and recorded before any person enters. A standby person stays at the access panel throughout. The ultrasonic set must be calibrated on the reference block at the start of each session and re-checked at the end; readings taken with an unverified calibration are void.
sections.procedure: 1. De-fuel the aircraft and purge the tank to the standard practice. WARNING: TANK ENTRY IS A CONFINED SPACE OPERATION. DO NOT ENTER UNTIL THE ATMOSPHERE TEST IS COMPLETE AND RECORDED, AND A STANDBY PERSON IS AT THE ACCESS PANEL. 2. Open the tank access panels in zones 531, 541 and 591. 3. Clean the run-out region of stringers 12 to 18 between ribs 8 and 14 and remove the sealant that covers the last three fastener rows. CAUTION: REMOVE THE SEALANT BY HAND SCRAPER ONLY. A POWERED TOOL WILL MARK THE STRINGER FOOT. 4. Calibrate the ultrasonic set on the reference block and record the calibration. 5. Starting at rib 8, scan the run-out of each stringer along the last three fastener rows. 6. Record the response at every fastener, whether or not it is above the reporting threshold. 7. Where a response is above the threshold, size the indication in both directions and record its position by stringer number and by fastener number. 8. Do a visual check of the stringer kit D5710124822382 and the lower spar cap kit D5710125087378 in the scanned region for any secondary damage. 9. Check the loop clamps EN26865-6B on the fuel quantity harness for security after the sealant removal. 10. Re-check the calibration on the reference block and confirm it has not drifted. 11. Restore the sealant over the scanned area to the standard practice.
sections.close_out: Close the tank access panels and do the fuel leak check. Do the fuel quantity system operational test. Send the completed recording sheet to the operator engineering department and, where the applicable service bulletin requires it, to Aeralis within ten days whether or not an indication was found.

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank until the atmosphere test is complete and recorded.
Keep a standby person at the access panel throughout.
Use only intrinsically safe lighting and equipment inside the tank.

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Ultrasonic inspection from inside the tank of the stringer run-out region between ribs 8 and 14 on the four-engine stretched aircraft, with the technique selected on the run-out standard and the fastener-by-fastener recording the fatigue assessment depends on.

sections.purpose: This task finds and sizes fatigue cracking at the run-out of stringers 12 through 18 on the wing lower cover between ribs 8 and 14, and records the result in the form the fatigue assessment needs.
sections.job_setup_note: This is a tank entry task. The aircraft must be de-fuelled and the tank purged, and the atmosphere test must be complete and recorded before any person enters. A standby person stays at the access panel throughout. The ultrasonic set must be calibrated on the reference block at the start of each session and re-checked at the end; readings taken with an unverified calibration are void. Technique note: this inspection is written against the parent lower cover thickness and reads the back wall echo at that thickness. A run-out that carries the bonded strap of the interim repair is locally thicker, the back wall moves out of the gate and an indication under the strap will not be seen at all with the standard setting. Where a strap is present, use the thick reference block from the tool set, move the gate to the strapped thickness and record on the sheet which block was used. A run-out at the reinforced standard is not inspected under this task at all.
sections.procedure: 1. De-fuel the aircraft and purge the tank to the standard practice. WARNING: TANK ENTRY IS A CONFINED SPACE OPERATION. DO NOT ENTER UNTIL THE ATMOSPHERE TEST IS COMPLETE AND RECORDED, AND A STANDBY PERSON IS AT THE ACCESS PANEL. 2. Open the tank access panels in zones 531, 541 and 591. 3. Establish the standard of every run-out to be scanned from the aircraft repair record and mark the strapped positions on the recording sheet before the sealant is touched. 4. Clean the run-out region of stringers 12 to 18 between ribs 8 and 14 and remove the sealant that covers the last three fastener rows. CAUTION: REMOVE THE SEALANT BY HAND SCRAPER ONLY. A POWERED TOOL WILL MARK THE STRINGER FOOT. 5. Calibrate the ultrasonic set on the reference block for the standard being scanned and record the calibration and the block used. 6. Starting at rib 8, scan the run-out of each stringer along the last three fastener rows. Change block and gate when the scan moves onto a strapped run-out; do not carry one setting across both. 7. Record the response at every fastener, whether or not it is above the reporting threshold. 8. Where a response is above the threshold, size the indication in both directions and record its position by stringer number and by fastener number. 9. Do a visual check of the stringer kit D5710124822382 and the lower spar cap kit D5710125087378 in the scanned region for any secondary damage. 10. Check the loop clamps EN26865-6B on the fuel quantity harness for security after the sealant removal. 11. Re-check the calibration on each block used and confirm it has not drifted. 12. Restore the sealant over the scanned area to the standard practice.
sections.close_out: Close the tank access panels and do the fuel leak check. Do the fuel quantity system operational test. Send the completed recording sheet, with the block used against each run-out, to the operator engineering department and, where the applicable service bulletin requires it, to Aeralis within ten days whether or not an indication was found.

type_data.effectivity_note: VTR-68R2 aircraft pre MOD-130450 only; the inspection is terminated by embodiment of the reinforcement

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank until the atmosphere test is complete and recorded.
Keep a standby person at the access panel throughout.
Use only intrinsically safe lighting and equipment inside the tank.
